original_value: In this paper, an adaptive fault tolerant control strategy is proposed to deal with the three pitch actuator faults in the large-scale wind turbines. Firstly, a simultaneous state and fault estimation was performed through a suitable LMI (linear matrix inequality) based optimal strategy. Hereafter, the new control law is designed using the previously estimated fault information. The actuator efficiency estimator uses as design parameters, respectively, the performance index γ against the wind and the learning rate Ξ. of the fault estimation algorithm. The study shows that the choice of the previous two parameters impacts the response time of the fault estimation and the correlation of the tracking error with the wind. The aim is to choose a small fault estimation response time while keeping a weak correlation between the tracking error and the wind turbulence noise. Finally, a tuning strategy is elaborated to choose the suitable γ and Ξ to match the reconfiguration objective.

result.paraphrase: This paper proposes an adaptive fault-tolerant control strategy for handling three pitch actuator faults in large-scale wind turbines. First, simultaneous state and fault estimation is carried out using a suitable optimal strategy based on an LMI (linear matrix inequality). Then, the new control law is designed from the previously estimated fault information. The actuator efficiency estimator is designed using the performance index γ against the wind and the learning rate Ξ of the fault estimation algorithm as parameters. The study shows that these two parameters affect the fault-estimation response time and the correlation between tracking error and wind. The goal is to obtain a short fault-estimation response time while maintaining a weak correlation between tracking error and wind turbulence noise. Finally, a tuning strategy is developed to select suitable γ and Ξ to meet the reconfiguration objective.
